questions.q: What does entity mapping on a Sentinel analytics rule actually do?
options: Changes how often the rule's query runs
Tells Sentinel which query column represents a real entity, such as an Account, Host, or IP address
Deletes columns from the query's results before an alert is generated
Controls which analysts are allowed to view the rule
questions.explain: Entity mapping turns a plain text or numeric column into a tracked entity Sentinel can follow across alerts.

questions.q: In an entity mapping, what is an "identifier"?
options: The name of the analytics rule itself
What a mapped column represents for that entity type, e.g. an Account's FullName or an IP's Address
The MITRE ATT&CK technique associated with the rule
A random unique ID Sentinel assigns to every alert
questions.explain: The identifier describes which attribute of the entity a given column maps to, such as FullName for an Account.

questions.q: What does entity mapping make possible that a rule without it cannot do?
options: Convert a scheduled rule into a built-in template
Automatically disable the data connector feeding the rule
Power the investigation graph and let Sentinel correlate incidents that share the same entity
Increase the rule's run frequency beyond 5 minutes
questions.explain: The investigation graph and cross-incident correlation both depend on entities being mapped in the first place.

questions.q: What does an incident look like when its generating rule has no entity mapping?
options: Automatically closed by Sentinel without analyst review
Identical to a mapped incident in every respect
Impossible to create — Sentinel requires entity mapping for every rule
Just raw query output as a flat table of columns, with no entity page or investigation graph to open
questions.explain: Without mapping, an alert is just text fields; there's no tracked entity to pivot from or correlate against.

questions.q: Two different analytics rules both flag the same user, but only one maps UserPrincipalName to an Account entity. What happens to Sentinel's ability to connect those two alerts?
options: Both alerts are merged into one incident regardless of mapping
Sentinel automatically links them anyway using the raw text value
The unmapped rule's alert is deleted automatically
Sentinel cannot recognize them as the same entity, since correlation requires both rules to map the same column to the same entity type
questions.explain: Correlation only works when both rules mapped the same column to the same recognized entity type.
